Task: Develop a complete lesson plan for teaching probability to high-school students.

Comprehensive Lesson Plan  
Topic: Introduction to Probability (High-School, Grades 9–10)  
Estimated Class Time: Two 55-minute periods (can be condensed to one 90-minute block)

────────────────────────────────────────
1. LEARNING GOALS
────────────────────────────────────────
Knowledge
• Define key probability terms: experiment, outcome, sample space, event, theoretical probability, experimental probability, complementary events, mutually exclusive events, independent events.  
• Calculate simple probabilities for equally likely outcomes.  
• Differentiate between theoretical and experimental probability.  
• Apply the addition rule P(A or B) and the multiplication rule P(A and B) for independent events.  

Skills
• Construct sample spaces (lists, tables, tree diagrams).  
• Collect and analyze data from a simulation/experiment.  
• Communicate reasoning using appropriate mathematical vocabulary.

Dispositions
• Appreciate how probability models real-world uncertainty.  
• Develop a habit of checking whether results are reasonable.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. STANDARDS ALIGNMENT (example: U.S. Common Core)
────────────────────────────────────────
CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.HSS.MD.A.1, HSS.MD.A.3, HSS.SCP.A.1, HSS.CP.A.1–5

────────────────────────────────────────
3. MATERIALS & PREP
────────────────────────────────────────
For each group (3–4 students):
• 1 six-sided die  
• 2 coins  
• Spinner template (paper clip & pencil) divided into 4 equal sections  
• Deck of 52 playing cards (optional extension)  
• Student handouts: Vocabulary sheet, Guided Notes, Practice Set, Exit Ticket  
• Chart paper / whiteboard markers  
Digital (optional): Virtual dice simulator, presentation slides

Teacher prep:
• Prepare slide deck with examples and animated tree diagrams.  
• Print/photocopy handouts.  
• Set up “Probability Stations” with labeled materials.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. LESSON SEQUENCE
────────────────────────────────────────
DAY 1 (55 min)

A. Warm-Up (5 min)
   • Quick poll: “What is more likely—rolling a 6 on a die or flipping heads on a coin?”  
   • Students justify answers; teacher notes vocabulary that will be formalized later.

B. Direct Instruction & Guided Notes (15 min)
   • Define experiment, outcome, sample space, event.  
   • Model creating a sample space for tossing a coin {H, T} and rolling a die {1–6}.  
   • Introduce theoretical probability P(E) = (# favorable outcomes)/(# total outcomes).  
   • Example calculation: P(rolling an even) = 3/6 = 1/2.  
   • Stress that probabilities run 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1 and complementary events sum to 1.

C. Cooperative Activity 1 – Station Rotation: “Theoretical vs. Experimental” (25 min)
   Station A: Coin toss (20 trials)  
   Station B: Die roll (36 trials)  
   Station C: Spinner (20 spins)  
   • Each group predicts probabilities theoretically, then runs trials, records data, and computes experimental probability.  
   • Groups post results on chart paper. Teacher circulates, probing with “Why do the experimental results differ?”

D. Synthesis & Debrief (8 min)
   • Whole-class comparison of theoretical vs. experimental results.  
   • Discuss Law of Large Numbers informally—experiments approach theoretical values as trials increase.  
   • Introduce homework: Finish reflection questions, read short article on real-life probability (sports analytics).

DAY 2 (55 min)

A. Do-Now / Quick Review (5 min)
   • Multiple-choice mini-quiz (3 items) on yesterday’s concepts.

B. Direct Instruction – Compound Events (15 min)
   • Mutually exclusive vs. non-exclusive events; addition rule: P(A or B) = P(A)+P(B)–P(A and B).  
   • Independent events; multiplication rule: P(A and B) = P(A)×P(B).  
   • Tree diagram of tossing two coins; find P(exactly one head).  
   • Example with cards: P(drawing a heart or a king).

C. Cooperative Activity 2 – “Probability Escape Room” (25 min)
   • Four locks require solutions:  
     1. Sample-space lock (tree diagram)  
     2. Addition rule lock  
     3. Multiplication rule lock  
     4. Challenge lock (combined rules)  
   • Students solve in groups; teacher provides hints for growth mindset.

D. Real-World Connection (5 min)
   • Short video clip (2 min) on probability in weather forecasting.  
   • Class: “If the weather app says 30% chance of rain, what does that mean?”

E. Exit Ticket & Closure (5 min)
   • Students individually solve:  
     1. P(rolling a number > 4 or an odd number) on a die.  
     2. P(getting two heads in two coin tosses).  
   • Write one lingering question about probability.

────────────────────────────────────────
5. DIFFERENTIATION & ACCOMMODATIONS
────────────────────────────────────────
• Provide sentence starters and word banks for ELL students.  
• Offer manipulatives (colored counters) for tactile learners.  
• Challenge extension: Conditional probability problem set.  
• Extra scaffolding: Pre-drawn tree diagrams with blanks for students needing support.  
• Large print handouts & verbal descriptions for visually impaired students.

────────────────────────────────────────
6. FORMATIVE & SUMMATIVE ASSESSMENT
────────────────────────────────────────
Formative
• Observations during stations/escape room  
• Exit tickets (Day 1 & Day 2)  
• Homework reflection

Summative
• Quiz (end of week) covering vocabulary, calculations, and applied scenarios.  
• Optional project: Students design and analyze their own probability game.

Rubric Snapshot (Quiz, 20 pts):  
Vocabulary (4 pts) – correct definitions.  
Computation (8 pts) – accuracy in probability calculations.  
Reasoning (4 pts) – explanation of steps.  
Application (4 pts) – interpreting real-world context.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. HOMEWORK & EXTENSIONS
────────────────────────────────────────
• Homework Day 1: Reflection + 10 practice problems (basic probability).  
• Homework Day 2: Compound events worksheet, including challenge question on card probabilities.  
• Extra credit: Use a free online simulator to run 1,000 coin flips; graph cumulative proportion of heads.

────────────────────────────────────────
8. REFLECTION & EVALUATION (Teacher)
────────────────────────────────────────
After lesson, note:
• Were students able to transition from single to compound probabilities?  
• Did station logistics allow enough trials?  
• Which misconceptions arose (e.g., “gambler’s fallacy”)?  
• Adjust pacing and add mini-lesson on conditional probability if many students advance quickly.

────────────────────────────────────────
9. SAFETY & ETHICS
────────────────────────────────────────
• Ensure coins/dice are not swallowed (appropriate for high school but still note).  
• Discuss ethical considerations of probability misuse (e.g., gambling addiction, misleading statistics).

────────────────────────────────────────
10. RESOURCES
────────────────────────────────────────
• Rossman/Chance Applet Collection (virtual experiments)  
• Khan Academy videos on basic probability  
• “The Joy of Statistics” BBC documentary excerpt  
• Cards, dice ordered from math manipulative catalogs

────────────────────────────────────────
11. GLOSSARY (for student handout excerpt)
────────────────────────────────────────
Experiment – an action with uncertain outcome.  
Outcome – result of a single trial.  
Sample Space – set of all possible outcomes.  
Event – subset of the sample space.  
Theoretical Probability – calculated likelihood assuming equally likely outcomes.  
Experimental Probability – ratio of observed favorable outcomes to total trials.  
Complementary Events – events whose probabilities sum to 1.  
Mutually Exclusive – events that cannot occur simultaneously.  
Independent Events – occurrence of one does not affect the other.

────────────────────────────────────────
END OF LESSON PLAN
